items.question: The app's take-profit leg is not reduce-only (a reduce-only TP was observed to make a stop trigger cancel both legs). The new once-a-second leg-size check can find the app's take-profit resting on the SAME side as the position (for example a sell take-profit while the account is short), so if it fills it ADDS to the position instead of closing it; the stop is reduce-only and sized for the old position. The owner already ruled that a take-profit resting while the account is flat is cancelled, then alerted. As built, the wrong-side case raises an urgent page and touches no order. What should the check do?

options.label: (a)
options.text: Cancel the wrong-side take-profit, then log red and send an urgent page saying it was cancelled; the same action the owner ruled for a take-profit resting while flat.

options.label: (b)
options.text: Alarm only, as built: red log, alert and urgent page; no order is touched; the owner cancels it by hand.

items.rationale: A wrong-side take-profit is the same hazard class as one resting while flat: an order that opens exposure with no stop covering it. The owner chose cancel-then-alert for the flat case and has said that loss bounds are not to be widened on grounds of rarity. (b) leaves the order live until the owner reacts to a page, and the owner is away for six weeks. (a) reuses the flat case's cancel path and its page, so it costs little. The case is rare (it needs a position flip or a manual mismatch), which is why the implementer chose alarm-only without a ruling.
